/-!
# Conjecture 10.5

by V. S. Anashin

Construct an example of a finite group whose mixed identities do not have a finite basis.
Is the group constructed in (R. Bryant, *Bull. London Math. Soc.*, **14**, no. 2 (1982),
119–123) such an example?

A *mixed identity* (identity with constants) of a group $G$ is an element $w$ of the free
product $G * F_\infty$, where $F_\infty$ is the free group on the countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$, such that $w$ becomes $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the
variables; equivalently, $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism $\varphi : G * F_\infty \to G$
that is the identity on $G$. A mixed identity $w$ is a *consequence* of a set $S$ of mixed
identities if $w$ lies in the smallest normal subgroup of $G * F_\infty$ containing $S$ that is
invariant under all endomorphisms of $G * F_\infty$ fixing $G$ elementwise (substitutions of
words for the variables). A *basis* of the mixed identities of $G$ is a set of mixed identities
of which every mixed identity of $G$ is a consequence.

Only the first sentence of the problem is formalised here. The second sentence asks about the
specific finite pointed group of R. M. Bryant, *The laws of finite pointed groups*, Bull. London
Math. Soc. **14** (1982), 119–123, whose laws with finitely many distinguished constants have no
finite basis.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.5
- V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*, Mat. Sb. (N.S.) **129(171)**
  (1986), no. 2, 163–174.
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: Monoid.Coprod (used as the free product), FreeGroup, MonoidHom.ker; no Mathlib notion of verbal/fully invariant subgroup or group laws exists (grepped for verbal, FullyInvariant, laws, variety).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.5».mixedIdentities
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of identities with constants (mixed identities) or of laws of a group. Defined as the subgroup ⨅ φ, φ.ker over all homomorphisms φ : G ∗ FreeGroup ℕ →* G with φ.comp inl = id, i.e. words vanishing under every substitution of elements of G for the variables.

blocks.name: mixedIdentities
blocks.text:
/--
The mixed identities of `G`: the words `w` in the free product `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` of `G`
with the free group on countably many variables such that `φ w = 1` for every homomorphism
`φ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* G` that is the identity on `G`. These form a subgroup of
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`.
-/
def mixedIdentities : Subgroup (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :=
  ⨅ φ : {φ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* G // φ.comp inl = MonoidHom.id G}, φ.1.ker

blocks.docstring:
The consequences of a set `S` of words in `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`: the smallest normal subgroup
of `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` containing `S` that is invariant under every endomorphism of
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` fixing `G` elementwise, i.e. under every substitution of words for the
variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Subgroup.normalClosure` (gives normality but not invariance under G-endomorphisms); no fully-invariant/verbal subgroup notion exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.5».mixedConsequences
justification.why_needed: The consequence closure of a set of mixed words: sInf of all normal subgroups of Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) containing B and invariant under every endomorphism ψ with ψ.comp Coprod.inl = Coprod.inl (substitution of words for variables). Needed to define 'basis'.

blocks.name: mixedConsequences
blocks.text:
/--
The consequences of a set `S` of words in `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`: the smallest normal subgroup
of `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` containing `S` that is invariant under every endomorphism of
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` fixing `G` elementwise, i.e. under every substitution of words for the
variables.
-/
def mixedConsequences (S : Set (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ))) : Subgroup (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :=
  sInf {N | N.Normal ∧
    (∀ σ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ),
      σ.comp inl = inl → ∀ w ∈ N, σ w ∈ N) ∧ S ⊆ N}

blocks.code:
def HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)), S.Finite ∧ mixedConsequences G S = mixedIdentities G
blocks.docstring:
The mixed identities of `G` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of words in
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` whose consequences are exactly the mixed identities of `G`. Such an `S`
automatically consists of mixed identities of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing analogous (finite basedness of laws) in Mathlib or the repo.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.5».HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis
justification.why_needed: 'The mixed identities of G have a finite basis': ∃ B : Finset (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)), ∀ w, IsMixedIdentity G w ↔ w ∈ mixedConsequences G B. (B ⊆ consequences B forces B to consist of mixed identities.)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_mixedIdentities_iff (w : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :
    w ∈ mixedIdentities G ↔
      ∀ v : ℕ → G, lift (MonoidHom.id G) (FreeGroup.lift v) w = 1 := by
  simp only [mixedIdentities, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, Subtype.forall]
  constructor
  · intro h v
    exact h _ rfl
  · intro h φ hφ
    have : φ = lift (MonoidHom.id G) (FreeGroup.lift (φ ∘ inr ∘ FreeGroup.of)) := by
      refine lift_unique hφ ?_
      ext n
      simp
    rw [this]
    exact h _

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mixedConsequences_mixedIdentities :
    mixedConsequences G (mixedIdentities G) = mixedIdentities G := by
  refine le_antisymm (sInf_le ⟨?_, ?_, le_rfl⟩) (le_sInf fun N hN => hN.2.2)
  · exact Subgroup.normal_iInf_normal fun φ => MonoidHom.normal_ker φ.1
  · intro σ hσ w hw
    simp only [mixedIdentities, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, Subtype.forall] at hw ⊢
    intro φ hφ
    have : (φ.comp σ).comp inl = MonoidHom.id G := by
      rw [MonoidHom.comp_assoc, hσ, hφ]
    exact hw (φ.comp σ) this

theorem hasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis_unit : HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis Unit := by
  refine ⟨{inr (FreeGroup.of 0)}, Set.finite_singleton _, le_antisymm ?_ ?_⟩
  · exact le_top.trans (le_of_eq (Subgroup.ext fun w => by simp [mem_mixedIdentities_iff]))

    have := hN (lift inl (FreeGroup.lift fun _ => w)) (by ext; simp) _ h0
    simpa using this

claims.decomposer_note: Formalize as the existence Prop: there is a finite group G whose set of mixed identities (elements w of the free product G * F_∞, e.g. `Monoid.Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`, with φ(w)=1 for every homomorphism φ : G * F_∞ → G restricting to the identity on G) is not the smallest normal subgroup closed under all G-fixing endomorphisms (substitutions of variables) containing some finite set; a candidate witness (Bryant's group) is asserted in the statement, so this is not a pure 'describe' request.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematically sound proposition: there is a finite group G (G : Type, Group G, Finite G) such that the subgroup of mixed identities of G in the free product G * F_∞ = Monoid.Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) (words killed by every homomorphism to G restricting to the identity on G; I checked in Lean that these are exactly the substitution evaluations Coprod.lift id (FreeGroup.lift v)) is not the smallest normal, G-fixing-endomorphism-invariant subgroup containing any finite set. /-!

by V. S. Anashin

specific finite pointed group of R. M. Bryant, *The laws of finite pointed groups*, Bull. London

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.5
- V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*, Mat. Sb. (N.S.) **129(171)**
  (1986), no. 2, 163–174.
-/

open Monoid Monoid.Coprod

namespace Kourovka.«10.5»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/--
The mixed identities of `G`: the words `w` in the free product `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` of `G`
with the free group on countably many variables such that `φ w = 1` for every homomorphism
`φ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* G` that is the identity on `G`. These form a subgroup of
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`.
-/
def mixedIdentities : Subgroup (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :=
  ⨅ φ : {φ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* G // φ.comp inl = MonoidHom.id G}, φ.1.ker

/--
The consequences of a set `S` of words in `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)`: the smallest normal subgroup
of `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` containing `S` that is invariant under every endomorphism of
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` fixing `G` elementwise, i.e. under every substitution of words for the
variables.
-/
def mixedConsequences (S : Set (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ))) : Subgroup (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :=
  sInf {N | N.Normal ∧
    (∀ σ : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) →* Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ),
      σ.comp inl = inl → ∀ w ∈ N, σ w ∈ N) ∧ S ⊆ N}

/--
The mixed identities of `G` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of words in
`Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` whose consequences are exactly the mixed identities of `G`. Such an `S`
automatically consists of mixed identities of `G`.
-/
def HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)), S.Finite ∧ mixedConsequences G S = mixedIdentities G

/-- A word is a mixed identity of `G` iff it vanishes under every substitution `v : ℕ → G` of
elements of `G` for the variables. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_mixedIdentities_iff (w : Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)) :
    w ∈ mixedIdentities G ↔
      ∀ v : ℕ → G, lift (MonoidHom.id G) (FreeGroup.lift v) w = 1 := by
  simp only [mixedIdentities, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, Subtype.forall]
  constructor
  · intro h v
    exact h _ rfl
  · intro h φ hφ
    have : φ = lift (MonoidHom.id G) (FreeGroup.lift (φ ∘ inr ∘ FreeGroup.of)) := by
      refine lift_unique hφ ?_
      ext n
      simp
    rw [this]
    exact h _

/-- A constant `g ∈ G` is a mixed identity of `G` iff `g = 1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem inl_mem_mixedIdentities_iff (g : G) : inl g ∈ mixedIdentities G ↔ g = 1 := by
  rw [mem_mixedIdentities_iff]
  simp

/-- Every set of words is contained in its consequences. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_mixedConsequences (S : Set (Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ))) :
    S ⊆ mixedConsequences G S :=
  fun _ hw => Subgroup.mem_sInf.2 fun _ hN => hN.2.2 hw

/-- The mixed identities of `G` are closed under consequences. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mixedConsequences_mixedIdentities :
    mixedConsequences G (mixedIdentities G) = mixedIdentities G := by
  refine le_antisymm (sInf_le ⟨?_, ?_, le_rfl⟩) (le_sInf fun N hN => hN.2.2)
  · exact Subgroup.normal_iInf_normal fun φ => MonoidHom.normal_ker φ.1
  · intro σ hσ w hw
    simp only [mixedIdentities, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, Subtype.forall] at hw ⊢
    intro φ hφ
    have : (φ.comp σ).comp inl = MonoidHom.id G := by
      rw [MonoidHom.comp_assoc, hσ, hφ]
    exact hw (φ.comp σ) this

/-- The mixed identities of the trivial group have the finite basis `{x₀}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis_unit : HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis Unit := by
  refine ⟨{inr (FreeGroup.of 0)}, Set.finite_singleton _, le_antisymm ?_ ?_⟩
  · exact le_top.trans (le_of_eq (Subgroup.ext fun w => by simp [mem_mixedIdentities_iff]))
  · refine le_sInf fun N ⟨_, hN, hS⟩ w _ => ?_
    have h0 : inr (FreeGroup.of 0) ∈ N := hS (Set.mem_singleton _)
    have := hN (lift inl (FreeGroup.lift fun _ => w)) (by ext; simp) _ h0
    simpa using this

/--
Construct an example of a finite group whose mixed identities do not have a finite basis.

Formalised as the existence of a finite group `G` such that the mixed identities of `G`, i.e.
the words in `Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ)` that vanish under every substitution of elements of `G` for
the variables, are not the consequences of any finite set of words.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.5» :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), ¬ HasFiniteMixedIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.5»

items: Variables: countably many, modelled by FreeGroup ℕ; the free product G * F_∞ is Monoid.Coprod G (FreeGroup ℕ) (notation G ∗ FreeGroup ℕ).

Mixed identity defined via arbitrary homomorphisms φ : G ∗ FreeGroup ℕ →* G with φ.comp inl = MonoidHom.id G, rather than via explicit substitutions v : ℕ → G; the API lemma `mem_mixedIdentities_iff` proves the two are equivalent.

Consequence closure requires both normality and invariance under all G-fixing endomorphisms (σ.comp inl = inl). Normality is not implied by endomorphism-invariance here (unlike in a free group), so it is stated explicitly. This agrees with the equational consequence relation for G-groups.
A basis is any set S with consequences S = mixed identities; S ⊆ consequences S holds automatically, so S consists of mixed identities. Finiteness is Set.Finite.

The primary slot is stated as a plain existence theorem (no answer(sorry)), following the decomposition notes, because the source is an imperative 'Construct an example' with a candidate witness asserted.
Category research open (the notebook marks the problem unsolved); G is taken in Type, with Finite G.
Three short proved @[category API] lemmas are included as sanity checks of the bespoke definitions (CONTRIBUTING asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions).
The module docstring cites Anashin's 1986 Mat. Sb. paper (without a URL) as the source of the terminology; a reviewer may wish to double-check the bibliographic details.

reviewer_notes: Modeling: mixed identities à la Anashin (all elements of G as constants, countably many variables), consequence = smallest normal subgroup invariant under all endomorphisms of G * F_∞ fixing G pointwise. Normality is imposed separately since G-fixing endomorphisms do not include conjugations. The equivalence between the homomorphism-based definition and substitution-based evaluation is proved in the file (mem_mixedIdentities_iff). Residual uncertainty is only about whether Anashin's original paper uses precisely this consequence relation (I argued it coincides with semantic consequence over G-groups for sets of mixed identities of G) and about the bibliographic details of the Anashin citation in the module docstring (Mat. Sb. 129(171) (1986) 163–174, taken from c06; I believe it is correct but could not verify offline). I deliberately omitted the Bryant DOI link proposed by c01 since it could not be verified. The final file compiles with `lake env lean` with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; the sandbox's lakefile.toml modification and run/ directory are pre-existing scaffolding, not mine.
